title: Authorizing a Custom Zscaler Connector for Salesforce

blocks.text: The Zscaler service supports custom, client-side connector onboarding for access to Salesforce. With this functionality, instead of requiring full administrator credentials, the Zscaler service can use a minimum set of credentials to access Salesforce.

When you create a custom connector for Salesforce for SSPM Scan, you must provide the client ID, client secret, integration user's username, and instance URL in the Zscaler Admin Console so that the Zscaler service can access the application. For Data Loss Prevention (DLP) and Malware scanning SaaS API onboarding, you additionally must include the Malware and DLP quarantine library names.
To create a custom connector for Salesforce:

blocks.item: Sandbox Tenant
1. Create a system administrator profile with a Salesforce license.
Log in to Salesforce.
In the left-side navigation, under Administration, click the Users drop-down menu and select Users.
Click New User.
See image.
The New User page appears.
On the New User page, enter all the required fields (marked with a red line next to them), selecting Salesforce for the User License, and System Administrator for the Profile.
Under General Information, deselect the following checkboxes:
Quick Access Menu
Salesforce CRM Content User
Receive Salesforce CRM Content Email Alerts
Receive Salesforce CRM Content Alerts as Daily Digest
Under Approver Settings, keep the Generate new password and notify user immediately checkbox selected.
See image.
Click Save. The email address you entered for the user receives an email to generate a password. Follow the instructions and save the password for future purposes.
2. Create permission set.
In the left-side navigation, under Administration, click the Users drop-down menu and select Permission Sets.
Click New.
See image.
The Permission Set Create page appears.
On the Permission Set Create page:
Label: Enter a name (e.g., Zscaler SaaS Integration Permission Set).
API Name: Enter a name (e.g., Zscaler SaaS Integration Permission Set API).
License: Select Salesforce.
See image.
Click Save.
Select either System Permissions or App Permissions depending on the required permissions found in the API Permissions section.
See image.
Click Edit to enable the ability to select the appropriate permissions, and click Save when done.
See image.
3. Assign permission set to admin user.
In the left-side navigation, under Administration, click the Users drop-down menu and select Users.
Select the admin user you created in the previous section.
Under Permission Set Assignments, click Edit Assignments.
See image.
The Permission Set Assignments page appears.
On the Permission Set Assignments page:
Available Permission Sets: Select the permission set you created previously.
Click Add. The permission set appears in the Enable Permission Sets section.
Click Save.
See image.
4. Create a new external client app.
In the left-side navigation, under the Apps drop-down menu, click App Manager.
Select New External Client App.
See image.
The External Client App Manager page appears.
On the External Client App Manager page, configure the following fields:
Enter the External Client App Name.
Enter an API Name.
Enter a Contact Email.
Select Distribution State as Local.
Select the Enable OAuth Settings checkbox.
Enter the following for Callback URL: https://test.salesforce.com.
Select the following OAuth Scopes:
Perform Requests at any time (refresh_token, offline_access)
Manage user data via APIs (api)
In the Flow Enablement section, select Enable JWT Bearer Flow.
Select Upload Files and upload the file that contains your digital certificate (e.g., salesforce.crt).
In the Security section, select Require secret for Web Server Flow and Require secret for Refresh Token Flow checkboxes.
See image.
Click Create.
The Manage External Client Apps page appears.
See image.
On the Manage External Client Apps page, configure the following fields under OAuth Policies in the Policies tab:
Permitted Users: Select Admin approved users are pre-authorized. Click OK in the Confirm permitted user policy window.
IP Relaxation: Select Relax IP restrictions.
Refresh Token Policy: Select Refresh token is valid until revoked.
Session Timeout In Minutes: Select 1,440 (24 hours).
See image.
Under App Policies, Select Profiles: Select Minimum Access - API Only Integrations.
See image.
Click Save.
5. Create libraries for quarantine policy actions. (DLP and Malware only)
If you are onboarding the tenant for DLP and Malware, you need to create two libraries for quarantine policy actions.
On the Salesforce homepage, go to the Files tab, select Libraries on the left menu, and click New Library.
To define library information:
Name: Enter Zscaler_Quarantine.
Unique Name: Enter Malware_Quarantine.
See image.
Click Save and Add Members, and the Manage Library Members window appears.
In the Manage Library Members window, add the system admin user you created earlier, set their permission to Library Administrator, and click Add.
See image.
Repeat steps a–d but enter Zscaler_DLP_Quarantine for the Name and DLP_Quarantine for the Unique Name.
6. Finish setup settings.
In the left-side navigation search box, enter Session Settings and click Session Settings.
Uncheck the Lock sessions to the IP address from which they originated checkbox and click Save.
See image.
In the left-side navigation search box, enter Salesforce CRM and select Salesforce CRM Content.
Check the Enable Salesforce CRM Content checkbox and click Save.
See image.
7. Generate private key file.

The custom onboarding process for Salesforce requires uploading your private key file to the Zscaler Admin Console. Zscaler recommends generating a certificate authority-signed (CA-signed) certificate which can be a more authoritative way to prove that your organization’s data communications are genuine. If you are unable to obtain the CA-signed certificate, a self-signed certificate can also be used. To learn more, refer to the Salesforce documentation.
You can extract the private key from the chosen CA certificate using one of the following methods:
Using Windows Certificate Manager:
Open the Run dialog (Win + R), enter mmc, and press Enter.
Go to File > Add/Remove Snap-in, select Certificates, and click Add.
Choose Computer account, click Next, select Local computer, and click Finish.
Go to Certificates (Local Computer) > Personal > Certificates.
Right-click your CA certificate, go to All Tasks, and select Export.
In the Export Wizard, select Yes, export the private key.
Choose Personal Information Exchange - PKCS #12 (.PFX) and enable Include all certificates in the certification path.
Set a secure password to protect the file, then save it to your local drive.
Extracting to a KEY file using OpenSSL:
When you have the PFX file, you can use OpenSSL to extract the key.
Open your terminal or command prompt and go to the folder with your .pfx file.
Run the following command to extract the private key. You are prompted for your PFX password.
openssl pkcs12 -in your_cert.pfx -nocerts -out private.key -nodes
Run the following command to extract the public certificate:
openssl pkcs12 -in your_cert.pfx -nokeys -out public_cert.pem
Upload the extracted key to the custom app using the Upload File link.
See image.
8. Copy Client ID and Client Secret.
In the left-side navigation search box, enter App in the search box and select App Manager.
Go to the app you previously created, click the drop-down arrow, and select View.
See image.
The Manage Connected Apps page appears.
On the Manage Connected Apps page, under API (Enable OAuth Settings), click Manage Consumer Details.
See image.
After receiving an email with a verification code, enter the code and click Verify.
In the next window, copy your Consumer Key, and the Consumer Secret. In the Zscaler Admin Console these are used for your Client ID and Client Secret.
9. Authorize the custom connector.
In the Zscaler Admin Console, from the navigation menu, go to Data Security > DSPM > SaaS Application Tenants.
Click Add SaaS Application Tenant.
See image.
Under Choose the SaaS Application Provider, select Salesforce.
In the Tenant Name field, provide a name.
See image.
Under Onboard SaaS Application for, select the checkbox for the functionality you want to enable.
See image.
Select Sandbox Account for the Tenant Type.
See image.
Under Authorize the SaaS Application:
SaaS Connector: Select Custom.
Enter the previously gathered information in these fields:
Client ID
Client Secret
Username of Integration User
Instance URL
Malware Quarantine Library Name (DLP and Malware onboarding only)
DLP Quarantine Library Name (DLP and Malware onboarding only)
See image.
Click Authorize.
(Optional) Under (Optional) Configure External Trusted Domains & User Profiles:

External Trusted Domains: Enter trusted email domains that are outside your organization (i.e., using a different domain). The Zscaler service views any email addresses from the added domains as trusted. For example, if your organization's domain is safemarch.com and your organization recently acquired a company with the domain example.com, you can add example.com to this list, and the service treats any email addresses from example.com (e.g., johnsmith@example.com) as internal users from safemarch.com. You can add up to 1,000 domains.

External Trusted Users: Enter trusted email addresses that are outside your organization (i.e., using a different email domain). The Zscaler service views the email addresses as trusted. For example, if your organization's email domain is safemarch.com and your organization recently contracted with someone using an external email domain (e.g., johnsmith@example.com), you can add the contractor's email to this list, and the service treats the contractor as an internal user from safemarch.com. You can add up to 1,000 email addresses.
See image.
In the Zscaler Admin Console, click Save and activate the change.

blocks.text: When creating custom connectors, provide the following application-specific API permissions to ensure that the Zscaler service has the access it needs.

blocks.item: API Permissions for Salesforce
In the following API tables, you need to select between the Sandbox and Production Tenants and select the appropriate permissions.
Sandbox Permissions Table
Instructions for adding permissions can be found in the Create permission set section for Sandbox tenants.

table: Manage Chatter Messages and Direct Messages
Modify Metadata Through Metadata API Functions

blocks.item: Production Permissions Table
Instructions for adding permissions can be found in the Create permission set section for Production tenants.

table: Manage Chatter Messages and Direct Messages
Modify Metadata Through Metadata API Functions
Read Access for Description, Subject, and Type Fields
